issues.failure_explanation: Densities do not carry over unchanged under the map (y,z,v) mapped to (u,v) with u = (y.odot y + z.odot z)^{1/2}: in polar coordinates dy_i dz_i = u_i du_i dtheta_i per coordinate, so for cylindrical p(t,y,z,v) = p~(t,u,v) the density of (u_t,v_t) is rho(t,(u,v)) = (2 pi)^d (prod_i u_i) p~(t,(u,v)), not p itself. The displayed equality is thus false as written (it already fails at t=0 for any nonconstant cylindrical initial density). The later use in Theorem thm_bndd_G is unaffected in conclusion, because the Radon-Nikodym ratios coincide: rho/pi = p~/pi~ under the coordinate lift, so the KL divergence is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The Burkholder-Davis-Gundy inequality gives E|int_0^T U_s dW_s|^q <= c E[(int_0^T U_s^2 ds)^{q/2}]; replacing the expectation of the power by the power of the integral of expectations requires E[U^q] < infinity (for q <= 2 Jensen's inequality is concave and gives the reverse bound). Here U_s = u_{1,s}^{epsilon-1}, so one needs E[u_{1,s}^{q(epsilon-1)}] = E[u_{1,s}^{-q(1-epsilon)}] < infinity, which part 1 of the same corollary provides only for q(1-epsilon) < 2; for q > 2/(1-epsilon) the inference is invalid and the stated conclusion 'for all q >= 1' is not established. \]

Hence, we have shown, for some constant $c$ depending on $\epsilon$ and $q$, that
\[
(\mathbb E \|u_t-u_s\|^q)^{1/q}\le c\,\abs{t-s}^{1/2-\epsilon}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate part 1 with the proved exponent, E||(u,v)_t - (u,v)_s||^q <= c_{q,epsilon} |t-s|^{q(1/2-epsilon)}; every subsequent application already uses epsilon-relaxed rates, so this suffices.
issues.overall_effect: The first displayed bound of Proposition timeregbnd is not established at the advertised exponent; all later uses (the residual estimates in Propositions prop:error_under_bounded_ball and prop:error_discrete) invoke only epsilon-relaxed rates, so a weakened statement suffices everywhere.
issues.title: Proposition timeregbnd(1) claims a 1/2 Hölder rate the proof does not deliver

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In terms of the density $p(t,\cdot)$ for \cref{cyl} and the Cartesian co-ordinates $\vec x_t\in \real^{3d}$, standard theory (Bakry--Emery criterion, Holley--Stroock theorem) applies to the potential $\frac 12 \lambda \|\vec x \|^2+G_3(\vec x)$, as it is a bounded perturbation (given by $G$) of a convex potential (given by $\frac12\lambda\|\vec x\|^2$).

We say $\pi_2$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality LSI$(R)$ if, for a constant $R>0$,
\[\mathcal{H}(\pi_1\mid \pi_2)\le\frac{1}{2\,R} \mathcal{I}(\pi_1\mid \pi_2),\qquad \forall \pi_1\ll \pi_2. 
\]

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's normalization LSI(R): H <= I/(2R), the Bakry-Emery/Holley-Stroock constant for pi proportional to exp(-beta(lambda||x||^2/2 + G_3(x))) is R = beta*lambda*exp(-beta(sup G - inf G)): the strongly convex part gives beta*lambda, and a bounded perturbation with oscillation omega enters the exponent multiplied by the inverse temperature beta. The stated R = beta*lambda*exp(-(sup G - inf G)) lacks this factor, so for beta > 1 the asserted decay exp(-2Rt/beta) in (hhh) is strictly faster than what the cited theory justifies and the displayed inequality is unproven (for beta < 1 it is merely conservative).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take R = beta*lambda*exp(-beta*(sup G - inf G)) (the Holley-Stroock constant at inverse temperature beta); (hhh) then holds verbatim with the corrected constant.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit geometric rate of Theorem thm_bndd_G is overclaimed for beta > 1; the qualitative geometric convergence and every later use, none of which depends on the numerical value of R, remain valid.
issues.title: Theorem thm_bndd_G: log-Sobolev constant R omits beta in the exponent
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction to the constant restores the theorem with the identical conclusion and no effect on any dependent result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Then, for any $T>0$, $E_{1,T}(\tstep)\to 0$ as $\tstep\to 0$ for
$$
E_{1,T}(\tstep)\eqdef
\tilde\pi_{\tstep}(P_{T}(\phi))-\pi_\tstep(\phi)+(\pi_\tstep-\tilde\pi_\tstep)(\phi),\qquad T=\tstep\,k.
$$

If the initial distribution is invariant for the Markov chain generated by the numerical method, so $\rho_0=\pi_\tstep$, we see that
$$
\lim_{\tstep\to 0}
\pi_{\tstep}(P_{T}(\phi))-\pi_\tstep(\phi)
\to 0,\qquad T=k\,\tstep.
$$

Then, we have 
\[
|\pi_{\tstep}(\phi)- \pi(\phi)|=\epsilon,\quad \tstep<\delta.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: With E_{1,T}(Dt) defined as tilde pi_Dt(P_T phi) - pi_Dt(phi) + (pi_Dt - tilde pi_Dt)(phi), the right-hand side of the pivotal identity equals 2 tilde pi_Dt(P_T phi) - tilde pi_Dt(phi) - pi(phi), not pi_Dt(phi) - pi(phi): the decomposition is algebraically false. Moreover the smallness of E_{1,T} is essentially the statement being proved (int (P_T phi - phi) d tilde pi_Dt does not vanish at fixed T without the very weak convergence under proof), and Theorem thm:num_conv is invoked for the initial law tilde pi_Dt although its hypothesis that rho_0/pi be uniformly bounded is never verified for the truncated measure (and would fail for pi_Dt itself). The final display also asserts |pi_Dt(phi) - pi(phi)| = epsilon instead of <= epsilon. The theorem is true: starting from any rho_tilde_0 much smaller than pi with bounded ratio (e.g. normalized pi restricted to a ball, whose V-moment is uniformly bounded by Lemma lem:2ndmoments_discrete), |pi_Dt(phi) - pi(phi)| <= |pi_Dt(phi) - P^k_Dt phi| + |E_{rho_tilde_0} phi((u,v)^k) - E_{rho_tilde_0} phi((u,v)_T)| + |P_T phi(rho_tilde_0) - pi(phi)|, handled by Theorem num_erg, Theorem thm:num_conv (with T = k Dt) and Theorem erg2 respectively.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second half of the proof by the standard three-term route: fix an initial law rho_tilde_0 much smaller than pi with bounded ratio and uniformly bounded V-moment, write |pi_Dt(phi) - pi(phi)| <= |pi_Dt(phi) - P^k_Dt phi| + |E_{rho_tilde_0}[phi((u,v)^k)] - E_{rho_tilde_0}[phi((u,v)_T)]| + |P_T phi(rho_tilde_0) - pi(phi)| and let the terms vanish via Theorem num_erg, Theorem thm:num_conv and Theorem erg2 respectively.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised convergence of the invariant measures pi_Dt to pi is asserted with an invalid proof; no other labelled result depends on it. The theorem itself survives with the paper's own ingredients (num_erg, thm:num_conv, erg2).
issues.title: The proof of Theorem thm_convergence_to_invariant is invalid
issues.why_classification: The theorem survives, but its central decomposition is algebraically wrong and the detour through the truncated measure is circular and unverifiable, so the argument must be rebuilt from existing tools: a contained restructuring with no mathematical loss, hence moderate rather than minor.
